newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's banking system needs urgent reform - govt.
newsitem.headline: Italy's banking system needs urgent reform - govt.

text.p: Italian banks faced a critical situation in terms of efficiency and urgent measures are needed to bring the system in line with other European countries, a statement from prime minister Romano Prodi's office said.
The note followed a meeting between the government and the Italian Banking Association.

Faced with the challenge of market globalisation, economic innovation and the single European currency, banks should start out on streamlining plans "to bring the Italian banking system in line with other European systems," the note said.

Bank of Italy governor Antonio Fazio has already warned of the banking system's low profitability and its need for restructuring, urging Italy's some 1,000 banking groups to cut their estimated 300,000 workforce by at least 10 percent.
The government said it will be consulting trades unions shortly for their views.
Representing the government at Tuesday's meeting were Labour minister Tiziano Treu, Treasury undersecretary Roberto Pinza and cabinet secretary Enrico Micheli.
